name: Golden Horde
summary: A Mongol khanate founded by Jochi’s line on the western steppe that dominated the Rus’ principalities for two centuries and later became Turkic and Muslim.

knownFor.label: Sarai
knownFor.note: The Horde’s capital on the lower Volga.

knownFor.label: Great Stand on the Ugra
knownFor.note: A stand-off traditionally seen as the end of Mongol rule over Russia.

location.value: The western steppe from the Danube to Siberia, ruling the Rus’ principalities as tributaries; capital Sarai on the Volga.
location.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

terrain.value: Open grassland of the Pontic–Caspian steppe and the Volga and Don river valleys.

climate.value: Continental steppe climate with harsh winters.

resources.value: Vast pastures for horses and sheep, plus control of trade routes.

disasters.value: The Black Death struck the Horde in the 1340s.

urbanisation.value: Sarai grew into one of the largest cities of its time; Genoese and Venetian ports lay on the Black Sea.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

disease.value: The plague spread from the Horde’s siege of Caffa (1346) to Europe.

economicBase.value: Herding, tribute from Rus’, and taxes on Silk Road and Black Sea trade.

tradeRoutes.value: Black Sea ports such as Caffa (Genoa) and Tana (Venice), and caravan routes to Central Asia.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: Pul, som, dirham; tribute from Rus’.

inequality.value: Mongol and Turkic aristocracy above herders, farmers and tributaries.

governmentType.value: A nomadic khanate ruled by descendants of Genghis Khan’s son Jochi.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

keyRulers.value: Batu Khan, Berke, Özbeg Khan (1313–1341), Tokhtamysh (1379–1395).

succession.value: Among Jochi’s descendants, decided by assemblies and often by force.

institutions.value: Collected tribute through Rus’ princes, who needed a khan’s patent (yarlyk) to rule.

stability.value: Strong until the “Great Troubles” (1359–1381), when many khans fought for power.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

eliteConflict.value: Many rival khans competed for the throne during the Great Troubles.
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

armyAndTech.value: Mounted archers organised in units of tens, hundreds and thousands.

majorWars.value: Conquest of Rus’ (1237–1241), war with the Ilkhanate, Battle of Kulikovo (1380), Timur’s invasion (1395–96).

alliancesRivals.value: Allied with the Mamluks against the Ilkhanate; rivals of Timur, Lithuania and later Moscow.

scienceEducation.value: Islamic scholarship grew after Özbeg Khan’s conversion.

religion.value: Tengrism and shamanism, then Islam from Özbeg Khan (1313), while tolerating Orthodox Christianity.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

languageWriting.value: Mongol for the court at first, then Kipchak Turkic; Uyghur script and Arabic script.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

artsArchitecture.value: Palaces, mosques and tiled buildings at Sarai, now mostly lost.

socialStructure.value: Khan, Mongol and Turkic nobles, herders, and settled subjects and tributaries.

sharedIdentity.value: Descent from Genghis Khan and, later, Islam.

neighbours.value: Rus’ principalities, Lithuania, Byzantium, the Ilkhanate, the Chagatai Khanate.

ideasReligions.value: Converted to Islam under Özbeg Khan.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

riseSignals.value: Batu’s conquest of Rus’ and the western steppe (1237–1241).

peakPeriod.value: Under Özbeg Khan (1313–1341), with rich trade and strong central rule.

declineSignals.value: The Black Death, the Great Troubles (1359–1381) and Timur’s invasion.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Golden Horde (checked 6 Nov 2026); Favereau, The Horde (2021)

outcome.value: Broke into khanates (Crimea, Kazan, Astrakhan); Sarai sacked in 1502.

sources.value: Rus’ chronicles and Arabic sources. Checked against Wikipedia (“Golden Horde”).

overallCertainty.value: Medium. The name itself is a later term.
